talks.title: BSides 2022 - Wolfgang Goerlich - And the Clouds Break: Continuity in the 21st Century
talks.teaser: Presents BSides 2022 - Wolfgang Goerlich - And the Clouds Break: Continuity in the 21st Century and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: Wolfgang Goerlich presents at BSides Cayman on business continuity and disaster recovery in the 21st century, reflecting on why zombie preparedness exercises didn't help during actual crises.

Key Topics: DR/BCP consulting experience in healthcare and financial services; zombie apocalypse preparedness kits as engagement tools; reaching out to organizations that didn't benefit from prior exercises; and modern continuity challenges.

Technical Details: Goerlich contacted organizations where he conducted creative BCP exercises—including zombie scenarios—only to discover they forgot the training during actual crises, revealing gaps between exercise engagement and operational retention.

Takeaways: Creative BCP exercises engage participants but don't guarantee crisis retention. Organizations need reinforcement mechanisms ensuring continuity knowledge persists beyond initial training events.

talks.title: BSides 2022 - Timothy Dilbert
talks.teaser: Analyzes BSides 2022 - Timothy Dilbert and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview:
Timothy Dilbert, CEO of BMT Solutions, presents at BSides Cayman 2022 on modern software development architectures, hybrid cloud deployment strategies, and identity governance. Dilbert explains how transitioning from legacy monolithic applications to decoupled microservices enhances both enterprise agility and intellectual property security. The talk details practical methodologies for satisfying stringent data residency regulations through hybrid cloud frameworks, establishing multi-cloud resilience, and replacing brittle Active Directory structures with modern identity governance.

Key Topics:
- Architectural comparison between monolithic systems and microservices
- Intellectual property protection through modular service outsourcing
- Hybrid and multi-cloud resilience using Red Hat OpenShift and niche cloud providers
- Modern Identity and Access Management (IAM), protocol federation, and automated recertification

Technical Details:
Dilbert contrasts traditional monolithic applications—where all user interface components, business logic, and database connections are packaged into a single, tightly coupled codebase—with microservices architectures. Using the human body's specialized subsystems (nervous, respiratory, digestive) as an analogy, he illustrates how decomposing large systems into isolated services accelerates development cycles. Crucially for security and intellectual property protection, microservices enable organizations to outsource specialized tasks (such as AI analytics engines or shareholder registry modules) to third-party contractors without exposing the underlying core codebase or proprietary business logic, preventing vendors from taking entire proprietary systems to competitors.

To navigate jurisdictional compliance challenges, such as offshore data residency and privacy mandates in the Cayman Islands, Dilbert advocates for hybrid cloud architectures. Platforms like Red Hat OpenShift allow organizations to containerize and pull traditionally cloud-hosted managed services down into localized on-premises data centers, maintaining direct oversight over hardware within approved legal boundaries. Furthermore, he emphasizes a multi-cloud operational model to mitigate vendor lock-in and systemic cloud outages, pairing specialized niche clouds to specific workloads—such as utilizing AWS for scalable S3 object storage, Microsoft Azure for Windows interoperability, and IBM Cloud for advanced predictive analytics and AI inferencing.

Turning to identity architecture, Dilbert warns against relying on legacy Active Directory (AD) for modern application authorization, describing how unmaintained AD groups inevitably become hazardous "boneyards" of forgotten privileges incompatible with macOS, iOS, and SaaS ecosystems. Instead, organizations must adopt modern identity federation protocols like OpenID Connect (OIDC) and SAML. He demonstrates replacing cumbersome, multi-step IT help desk ticketing chains with automated IAM launchpads where business application owners directly approve role-based access requests. Finally, Dilbert highlights automated IAM governance features, including outlier detection algorithms that flag accounts with excessive privileges relative to peers, and automated recertification campaigns executed by internal audit to systematically revoke lingering permissions across both business units and IT personnel.

Key Takeaways:
Adopting microservices protects intellectual property during external development by isolating specialized modules from core source code. Deploying hybrid container platforms like OpenShift enables organizations to leverage cloud-native services while maintaining strict jurisdictional data residency compliance on-premises. Enterprises must phase out legacy Active Directory authorization in favor of modern OIDC/SAML federated identity governance featuring automated access recertification and algorithmic outlier detection.

talks.title: BSides 2022 - Adam Pennington - Bringing Intelligence into Cyber Deception with MITRE ATT&CK
talks.teaser: Examines BSides 2022 - Adam Pennington - Bringing Intelligence into Cyber Deception with MITRE ATT&CK and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Deception in context

MITRE ATT&CK lead Adam Pennington defines cyber deception as causing adversaries to accept false information, tracing roots from Sun Tzu and WWII (Double Cross, Operation Mincemeat) through Cliff Stoll's Cuckoo's Egg honeypot and the Honeynet Project to today's commercial deception market.

Defensive value

Deception increases adversary ambiguity about stolen data, network location, and target validity. It supports detection (honeypots, honey tokens) and intelligence gathering in fake environments. He cites France's 2017 Macron campaign planting decoy emails to discredit leaked material after the 2016 DNC hack.

Frameworks and planning

He introduces MITRE Engage for goals like exposure, affecting behavior, and elicitation, mapped to deception categories and techniques. Pennington stresses matching deception maturity to adversary knowledge, prioritizing MFA and patching first, and using ATT&CK to plan intelligence-driven deception rather than product pitches.

talks.title: BSides 2022 - David Manouchehri
talks.teaser: Examines BSides 2022 - David Manouchehri and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## From Botnets to Home Routers

David Manouchehri, an independent researcher known for Chrome zero-days, connects the Miri IoT botnet to ISP modem insecurity. Miri spreads by scanning random IPv4 addresses on ports 22 and 23—a crude method that still works at scale.

## Command Injection on Modems

Manouchehri discloses local command injection on consumer modems that should never expose a shell to subscribers. While not remotely reachable by default, anyone on the LAN can execute operating-system commands through the flaw.

## A Cautionary Remediation Tale

After reporting, the ISP changed Telnet from port 23 to 23.23 and applied IPv4-only firewall rules blocking ports 22 and 23. Because IPv6 rules differed, the service became reachable over IPv4 as well—and Telnet ended up exposed to the internet on port 23, worsening the issue.

## Lessons

The talk underscores how rushed fixes create new exposures, why IPv6 parity matters in firewall policy, and how consumer CPE remains a soft target that enables botnets like Miri despite its unsophisticated propagation strategy.
